title: Why Do Sprouting Peas Get Warm?

scenes.tts: Why can sprouting peas warm a thermos, while boiled peas cannot? Peas have no muscles. Both thermoses begin near room temperature. Only one contains living cells. Watch the warmth rise as we follow stored food energy through one pea cell.
scenes.visual: Hook first. Two large cutaway thermoses fill the frame, labelled 'sprouting peas' and 'boiled, cooled peas'. Their thermometer columns begin together; the sprouting column slowly rises while the other holds. Keep a small 'schematic' label on every cartoon throughout. Establish the shared COLOUR MAP: glucose blocks GOLD, oxygen dots BLUE, carbon dioxide blocks GREY, water drops CYAN, energy for cell work GREEN, thermal energy ORANGE, mitochondria PURPLE, cells CREAM.
scenes.narration: Why can sprouting peas warm a thermos, while boiled peas cannot? Peas have no muscles. Both thermoses begin near room temperature. Only one contains living cells. Watch the warmth rise as we follow stored food energy through one pea cell.

scenes.tts: Inside the sprouting pea, food molecules store energy. The fuel we will follow is glucose. Glucose is a sugar that stores energy in its molecules. Plants make glucose by photosynthesis. Cells must release stored energy before using it.
scenes.visual: The sprouting thermos stays at left while one pea enlarges into a CREAM plant-cell cartoon. A store labelled 'food molecules' sends GOLD blocks marked 'glucose' into the cell. A small sunlight-to-leaf-to-glucose strip transforms into the GOLD blocks; no molecular structure appears.
scenes.narration: Inside the sprouting pea, food molecules store energy. The fuel we will follow is glucose. Glucose is a sugar that stores energy in its molecules. Plants make glucose by photosynthesis. Cells must release stored energy before using it.

scenes.tts: Cellular respiration releases that energy. Glucose and oxygen enter the pathway. Carbon dioxide and water leave, along with released energy. Oxygen is a gas cells use. Carbon dioxide is a gas they give off.
scenes.visual: Within the carried cell, a wide pathway opens. GOLD glucose blocks and drifting BLUE oxygen dots move in from the left. GREY carbon-dioxide blocks, CYAN water drops, and a bright energy stream move out right. The word equation builds above using labelled blocks only.
scenes.narration: Cellular respiration releases that energy. Glucose and oxygen enter the pathway. Carbon dioxide and water leave, along with released energy. Oxygen is a gas cells use. Carbon dioxide is a gas they give off.

scenes.tts: Respiration happens in many small steps, not one burst. The first steps occur in the cytoplasm. Most of the work follows inside mitochondria. Plant and animal cells both have these small organelles. Fungus cells usually have them too.
scenes.visual: The pathway divides into stepping-stones. The first few glow in the CREAM cytoplasm; the rest flow into a large PURPLE mitochondrion. A small plant cell, animal cell, and yeast cell slide in beside it, each showing PURPLE mitochondria. Everything is labelled 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Respiration happens in many small steps, not one burst. The first steps occur in the cytoplasm. Most of the work follows inside mitochondria. Plant and animal cells both have these small organelles. Fungus cells usually have them too.

scenes.tts: Do not confuse mitochondria with chloroplasts. Chloroplasts let a plant make glucose by photosynthesis. Mitochondria let plant and animal cells release stored food energy. A plant cell can contain both kinds of organelle.
scenes.visual: Keep the plant cell large. A GREEN chloroplast makes GOLD glucose blocks on the left; a PURPLE mitochondrion receives those blocks on the right. Short labels read 'chloroplast: make food' and 'mitochondrion: release stored energy'. Both organelles drift gently in the cytoplasm.
scenes.narration: Do not confuse mitochondria with chloroplasts. Chloroplasts let a plant make glucose by photosynthesis. Mitochondria let plant and animal cells release stored food energy. A plant cell can contain both kinds of organelle.

scenes.tts: The pathway has released stored energy. Where will that energy go now? Will it power cell work, leave as warmth, or do both? Make your prediction.
scenes.visual: The energy stream reaches a fork inside the carried cell. Three large choices appear: GREEN gear 'cell work', ORANGE moving particles 'warmth', and both arrows together. The question stays centred while both possible branches pulse faintly.
scenes.narration: The pathway has released stored energy. Where will that energy go now? Will it power cell work, leave as warmth, or do both? Make your prediction.

scenes.visual: Deliberate predict pause. Hold the three choices and question. A ring timer drains smoothly while GOLD energy waits at the fork.

scenes.tts: It does both. One branch powers cell work, such as building new cell parts. Another becomes thermal energy, the motion of particles we feel as warmth. Some released energy always leaves along this thermal branch.
scenes.visual: Reveal both branches. GREEN energy turns a large gear that assembles a new cell part. ORANGE energy spreads into particles whose motion visibly quickens. The choices collapse into one moving split diagram that fills the frame.
scenes.narration: It does both. One branch powers cell work, such as building new cell parts. Another becomes thermal energy, the motion of particles we feel as warmth. Some released energy always leaves along this thermal branch.

scenes.tts: The cell did not make new energy. It changed energy already stored in glucose. The thermos slows the orange thermal energy from escaping. As living pea cells keep respiring, their thermometer can rise.
scenes.visual: The GOLD stored-energy glow transforms into GREEN work and ORANGE particle motion; a red cross covers 'new energy'. The cell shrinks back into the sprouting thermos. ORANGE particles bounce from the insulated wall instead of leaving, and its thermometer rises slowly. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: The cell did not make new energy. It changed energy already stored in glucose. The thermos slows the orange thermal energy from escaping. As living pea cells keep respiring, their thermometer can rise.

scenes.tts: Breathing is different from cellular respiration. Breathing moves air into and out of lungs. It brings oxygen in and carries carbon dioxide out. Respiration happens inside cells, including cells in organisms without lungs.
scenes.visual: The pea-cell pathway stays visible at right. At left, a runner's lungs expand and contract as BLUE oxygen enters and GREY carbon dioxide exits. A divider labels 'breathing: lungs' and 'respiration: cells'; a seed and yeast cartoon appear under 'no lungs'.
scenes.narration: Breathing is different from cellular respiration. Breathing moves air into and out of lungs. It brings oxygen in and carries carbon dioxide out. Respiration happens inside cells, including cells in organisms without lungs.

scenes.tts: Now compare the thermoses again. Sprouting peas contain living cells that keep releasing thermal energy. Boiling killed the cells in the control peas. After those peas cool, they do not respire, so their thermometer stays near the room.
scenes.visual: Return to the original thermos pair. Tiny carried pathways animate throughout the sprouting peas; ORANGE motion accumulates. The boiled, cooled peas show crossed-out pathways and a steady thermometer aligned with a 'room' marker. Label the whole comparison 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Now compare the thermoses again. Sprouting peas contain living cells that keep releasing thermal energy. Boiling killed the cells in the control peas. After those peas cool, they do not respire, so their thermometer stays near the room.

scenes.tts: Respiration releases stored food energy for cell work and as thermal energy. That explains the warmth without inventing energy. Next, temperature, oxygen, and sugar will change its rate around the same pathway.
scenes.visual: The thermos pair transforms into the pea-cell pathway. The line 'Respiration releases stored food energy for cell work and as thermal energy.' types on once above it. Three controls settle around the pathway: a thermometer, an oxygen valve, and a GOLD glucose supply. They move gently but do not reveal their effects.
scenes.narration: Respiration releases stored food energy for cell work and as thermal energy. That explains the warmth without inventing energy. Next, temperature, oxygen, and sugar will change its rate around the same pathway.

scenes.visual: End card with one line only: 'Respiration releases stored food energy for cell work and as thermal energy.'
